sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are run on the same finite interval \(\Lambda_n\), with a prespecified washout and a fixed-width interior buffer.
sampling_model.units: One realization of a stationary radius-\(r\) innovation network on \(\mathbb Z\), observed through \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzed on \(I_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments \(D_i^{(1)}\) and \(D_i^{(2)}\) enter the same local exposure maps and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensities are known from the design. The statistic estimates only the two wave means \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^{(2)}\); it does not estimate \(m_i\) or fit a regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 show that zero asymptotic variance for a stationary finite-variance finite-dependent sequence is equivalent to a finite-dependent coboundary and yields an unnormalized endpoint-difference law.
The paper proves consistency and asymptotic normality for exposure-IPW estimators under approximate neighborhood interference and studies network-HAC inference for one randomized finite population.
The paper proves central limit and invariance principles for stationary fields represented as functions of independent innovations under short-range physical dependence.
The paper proves treatment-effect asymptotics under graphon-random interference and develops direct- and indirect-effect inference.

The preprint proves asymptotic normality and optimality for regression-adjusted average-direct-effect estimators under graphon interference and consistently estimates the linear estimator's asymptotic variance under a low-rank graphon condition.

body.tldr: Two independent assignment waves on one buffered F\o lner interval turn the latent Palm population covariance into an observable cross-wave IPW moment. The statistic \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\) uses only the two wave scores and their sample means, obeys an explicit uniform finite-sample concentration inequality, and yields a level-\(\alpha\) test of \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) with uniformly guaranteed power at the derived \(n^{-1/2}\) separation scale. Janson2015 supplies the finite-block coboundary and endpoint law as known substrate; the theorem-level contribution is the repeated-randomization diagnostic, not a causal relabeling of that probability result.

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 exactly classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, while existing network-interference papers analyze effect estimation or variance estimation from one randomization. None supplies an observable, uniformly size-controlled test of whether the Palm population component itself vanishes.
project_justification.niche: Repeated online randomization on the same local network makes cross-wave IPW products conditionally remove assignment noise, converting the latent boundary into a directly estimable finite-lag functional.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the complete two-wave statistic and nuisance means, proves an explicit concentration inequality, derives finite-sample size and power guarantees at an attainable root-sample-size separation, and leaves only the sharp minimax rate as open content.

body.related_work: Janson2015 is the primary mathematical comparator. Its Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 already give the finite-dependent zero-variance, block-factor coboundary, and endpoint-difference laws, so those results enter only as cited substrate for interpreting the null. Leung2022ANI supplies the one-wave exposure-IPW framework and approximate-neighborhood-interference perspective, but its finite-population target and network-HAC estimator differ from the two-wave Palm population-variance diagnostic. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-mapping and known-propensity design foundation, not a repeated-wave population-covariance test. ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013 informs the iid-innovation representation; no new central limit theorem is claimed against it. LiWager2022 studies direct and indirect effects under a generally dense graphon-random model, whereas the diagnostic here uses a fixed-radius sparse local score and two assignments on the same realized environment. FanLengWu2025 uses a possibly sparse graphon, restricts its consistent linear-estimator variance formula to a low-rank graphon, targets the average direct effect, and estimates the asymptotic variance of its regression-adjusted estimator. The present target is instead the zero boundary of the Palm covariance component of a local exposure-IPW score, and its estimator is the regression-free cross-wave covariance statistic \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to the same no-carryover potential-outcome schedule. The single-wave BondEtAl2012 experiment cannot be reanalyzed with this diagnostic. The finite-radius restriction and ambient interval lags are deliberate: the proposal does not assert approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, random-radius stabilization, graph-distance HAC consistency, or unchanged-HAC exactness.
body.honest_scope: The observable cross-wave identity, uniform concentration bound, and size--power theorem are the proposed results. Janson's finite-block coboundary and endpoint law are published inputs and carry no novelty claim. The minimax optimality of the derived \(n^{-1/2}\) separation rate remains open. As a cited sanity check, homogeneous conditional effects give \(h_i=0\) and lie on the zero side, consistent with assignment-dominated cases discussed by LiWager2022; Proposition 3 shows that homogeneity is not necessary.
